nodes.name: Calle Jorge white tiled benches
nodes.source: IMG_2182, IMG_2229, IMG_2230 and IMG_2234 look along Calle Jorge: about four square terracotta tiles across (0.36 m each), joints running with the path and not on the diagonal, a pale concrete edge, then lawn. Lawn side: the lawn runs from the path to the house fronts (the aerial shows it from about 95 to 127 m). IMG_2182 and IMG_2229 show a two-tile cross-path with the same pale edge leaving the lane about 1.9 m east of the bench (read from the tile rows and the horizon in both photos), and IMG_2229 and IMG_2231 show a second path that leaves the lane about 4 m west of the bench, runs diagonally behind it and on along the house front past a white-kerbed bed with three round clipped shrubs and a strelitzia, with a climber trained on the wall behind; a smaller kerbed shrub stands on the lawn west of the bench (the aerial shows its white kerb at about 106.5 m). Where the paths run between the lane and the houses is estimated to about 1 m. IMG_2231 and IMG_2232 are the bench, IMG_2596 the path beside it with a round red SANEA cover and a square grate; IMG_2231 also shows house number 20. The one photographed bench is the station at 112 m; no photo shows a second bench, and three more are placed from the aerial (see benches.aerialBasis). IMG_2234 shows the CALLE DE TEODORO plaque on the lawn-side wall with a bougainvillea over it, a tall clipped hedge on the lawn in front, yellow lantana behind the hedge, a green round cover in the grass, and slot drains and square grates across the path where the octagon-tiled lane of IMG_2235 joins from the hedge side. Hedge side, from west to east: a white planter wall with a clipped hedge standing at the path edge (IMG_2234); the octagon-tiled lane (the mapped Teodoro Rojo line at 93.4 m); then an open garden lawn edged by a white-painted kerb that turns back along that lane, with one black lamp post on the kerb corner (IMG_2234, IMG_2235) and a dragon tree on the lawn near the lane (IMG_2230, IMG_2182). IMG_2183 and IMG_2233 are taken across that lawn, which is open to the lane with no wall or hedge in front: the candelabra tree stands towards the back, a few pale trunks and a broad crown of curved, winged stems about twice the height of the garden wall behind it, over a bed of lantana, with a bougainvillea trained along that wall. Its 5.6 m height, 4.2 m spread and place on the lawn are estimates. East of the garden the planters resume in front of the patios (IMG_2182, IMG_2230): about 0.7 m high, a clipped hedge in each, broken by two brick-paved thresholds about 1.1 m wide with a short planter between them; a small recess with a blue-and-white number tile sits by each threshold (the digits are not legible, so none are modelled). Gap stations are read from the pins and are good to about 2 m. Only one lamp post is seen along the lane (the kerb corner); IMG_2234 shows wall lanterns, not posts, further west, so the posts formerly at 88, 92 and 118 m were removed. IMG_2597 is the CALLE DE JORGE plinth and black lamp at the east end, standing on a lawn with an old olive beside it; the plinth's lettered face is turned towards the path and the camera (south-west), not along the lane. Lawn, wall and planting are not continued between the west entrance (see west, to about 28 m) and the photographed east stretch. Pins are ±2 to ±5 m and no camera is solved, so every station here is an estimate.

nodes.name: Calle Jorge west entrance: flagged path, white kerbs, lamp, lawns, round trees and shrub border
nodes.source: IMG_2280 and IMG_2696-2698 stand in the Pintor Dalí car park at the west end of the mapped Calle Jorge line and look east-north-east along it (headings 56 to 65 degrees; the line runs 60). They show a path of irregular sandstone flags about 2 m wide between two white-painted kerbs the length of the parking bays, the left kerb ending in a short return beside a black lamp post that carries a camera, then lawn on both sides with the flagged path running on to a white gateway. Two round clipped trees stand on the left (north) lawn; on the right a border of clipped and yellow-flowering shrubs runs along a house with a purple bougainvillea over its first floor. The aerial agrees: parked cars to about 7 m, a 9 m deep lawn with two tree crowns on the north side, a house 3.4 m off on the south side, and a white mark on the line at about 28 m read as the gateway. The flags are built to 28 m; the gateway itself, and whether flags or terracotta lie beyond it, are not known. Kerb length, path width and plant positions are estimated to about 1 m; no camera is solved.

nodes.name: Lantana planter wall along Calle Guillermo behind the Calle de Jorge plinth
nodes.source: IMG_2773 looks up Calle Guillermo from the Jorge junction and IMG_2774 from 9 m further on: a neat, straight white planter wall about a metre high (waist height beside the lane), about 0.45 m thick, with a low dense carpet of orange and yellow lantana along its top, runs along the lane's east side to the steps of the pool building. A clump of spiky yucca or dragon-tree heads rises from behind it about a third of the way along; there is no palm beside it. IMG_2597 shows the same wall behind the lawn of the CALLE DE JORGE plinth. The wall's top is set one metre above the lane surface beside it. It is built from 3 to 25 m north of the Jorge line; IMG_2822 and IMG_2823 show it also continues south past the junction and round towards the sea, which is not built.

nodes.name: Tall slender palm on the main-pool lawn below Calle Jorge
nodes.source: IMG_2764 and IMG_2765 look across the main-pool lawn from below Calle Jorge: tall slender palms, the trunk three to four times the height of a compact crown, stand on the lawn towards the pool, the nearest about 19 m from the camera on a bearing of about 330 degrees (it is left of centre in IMG_2764 and just right of centre in IMG_2765; the distance is read from where its foot meets the lawn). It replaces two short, thick generic palms: one that stood against the Guillermo planter (object enrique-steps-4), where IMG_2773 shows a yucca clump and no palm, and one 5 m in front of this camera (main-pool-2), where IMG_2764, IMG_2765 and IMG_2598 show open lawn. Position is good to about 4 m; the 15 m height follows from that distance. Moved 2026-11-13 (Dave asked which side of the palm the path runs): the georeferenced aerial shows its crown at about (-23.4, 106), just west of where the pink path meets the pool deck, so the path runs on the palm's right seen from the gate, as IMG_2764 and IMG_2603 show; the camera is about 30 m from it, not 19 m, which makes it about 20 m tall. A tall crown can sit a metre or two off its foot on an aerial. Moved again 2026-11-19 (Dave: the palm is on the wrong side of the path): IMG_2765, IMG_2764, IMG_2603 and IMG_3076 all show the trunk standing in its own bed on the RIGHT of the pink path where it reaches the pool deck, seen from the gate, with the path passing on its left and bending left to the steps. The 13 Nov reading had the sides swapped. It stood 1.8 m right of the path centreline at its end, which put the trunk on the widened pink paving there (Dave's Inspect screenshot, 19 Nov: wrong place). Rechecked in IMG_2765: the palm and the bin by the path stand on the same line of sight, the palm about 3 m beyond the bin, and the palm is about 4 degrees right of where the path ends; that puts the foot at (-18.6, 106.3), on the lawn edge 2 m from the path centreline, 0.8 m clear of the paving, as IMG_3076 shows it in its own bed beside the path. The aerial crown position is not used for the foot.

nodes.name: Calle Guillermo paving beside the planter: squares at the junction, octagons beyond, covers
nodes.source: IMG_2773 and IMG_2774 look up Calle Guillermo from the Jorge junction: the lane is paved wall to wall, about 2.3 m wide between the plinth lawn and the planter, in large terracotta squares at the junction and then, from about 3 m north, in terracotta octagons with small square insets (five or six across), on towards the steps of the pool building. A round cast cover and two rectangular grates lie in the octagons. IMG_2822 and IMG_2823 show the same octagons south of the junction. In IMG_2773 the squares are about 1.4 times the octagon pitch, so they are drawn 0.56 m against 0.4 m octagons; the real sizes are not known. The paving is laid from 5 m south to 25 m north of the Jorge line (squares for the 6 m up to 3 m north) on the mapped Guillermo line, against the planter's lane face, which closes the grass strip the model had between wall and lane. Width and cover positions are estimated to about 0.5 m.

nodes.name: West of Calle Guillermo: plain lawn wall, patio wall, hedged planters, lamp posts and brick border
nodes.source: Dave, 2026-11-12: from the IMG_2773 viewpoint the houses on the left do not match the photo. IMG_2773 and IMG_2774 show, west of Calle Guillermo: the plinth lawn with a small broad-leaved tree and a rose bush; along the lawn's north side a plain white wall with no door or window, bougainvillea trained along it, its top falling from well over a storey high on the left to about 2.6 m at the lane (6.6 times the 0.4 m sign plate, and 2.8 m against the 3.8 m lamp post), where it ends in a pier carrying a no-dogs sign near its top; then, along the lane, low white planters with clipped hedges, broken by gateways, with a taller white patio wall behind them, strelitzia leaves showing above it and two lamp posts; a row of bricks on edge borders the lane. The houses stand back behind these walls, with chimneys showing. The wall along the lawn lies on the registry edge of part 6364401UF1366S_part7 (11 m north of the Jorge line). Dave agreed on 12 November to treat that part's east portion as an open walled patio on the photo evidence (data/registry_corrections.json, openPatios), so the lawn wall is now one wall from the west block's corner to the lane, its top falling from 3.9 m to 2.6 m (a one-photo estimate: the wall is about 3.9 m at the left of the frame if the sign plate is 0.4 m and the lamp post 3.8 m), with the patio's other sides walled at 2.1 m on the registry lines and strelitzia showing above. The planters, patio wall and lamp posts stand on ground the registry leaves empty, where the aerial shows walled patios. Where the roofed west block ends is not seen in any photo. Planter, gateway and lamp positions are read from the two photos and good to about 1.5 m; the patio wall's position is good to about 1 m.

nodes.name: Calle Jorge garden planting: small trees, bougainvillea in bract, west-entrance shrub border, lawn colour
nodes.source: Read 2026-11-13. IMG_2229 and IMG_2230 show, against the house-23 front on the lawn side, a small grey-green tree about 3.5 m high beside the kerbed bed and a tall bougainvillea in full purple bract at the house corner; the bougainvilleas on these walls are masses of colour, not green climbers. IMG_2697 shows the house on the south side of the west entrance covered to first-floor height in purple bougainvillea, and a row of low clipped shrubs along the north edge of the flagged path under the round trees. IMG_2773 shows a small light-green broad-leaved tree on the plinth lawn (replacing the dark generic tree first put there) and climbers spilling over the top of the lawn wall. The lawns in all of these are a darker, more olive green than first modelled (sampled about RGB 105,110,66 in the overcast photos), and the bracts a duller violet-pink than pure magenta. Positions are read from the photos and good to about 1.5 m; trees and shrubs are Details.

nodes.name: Calle Jorge gateway at the end of the flagged path, with its walls and cross-path

nodes.name: Barraka restaurant: parapet, clerestory windows, door, glazed awnings and thatched edge
nodes.source: Wall height: on IMG_2618 the parapet is about 2.4 times the black door. Taking the door as 2.05 m gives a wall of about 4.9 m; the model uses 4.8 m. The 2014-15 laser survey records this roof at a median of 2.89 m and a high point of 3.67 m (docs/reviews/lidar-levels, 6364501UF1366S_part8), below the photographed parapet. That survey figure is kept as the roof deck or an older roof, not as a reason to squash the clerestory into the registry's 3 m storey. The ring is not moved. North-east openings are read from the square-on IMG_2618 (pin +-2.4 m, camera not solved): two groups of three brown-framed windows, not the three groups of three the task brief counted; IMG_2615 is the same wall seen obliquely. The door is under the landward group. The louvred vent sits in the parapet between the groups; the small slot vent below the timber band is the second vent in IMG_2615 and its station is the less certain of the two. South-west: IMG_2604 shows eight clerestory windows, two red scalloped awnings, glazing, frosted BARRAKA BEACH lettering, a thatched eaves and a rooftop tank. North-west: IMG_2630 and IMG_2611 show glazing and one awning on the west corner, then a plain wall with one small window. Stations along the walls are estimates of about a metre. Lettering, scallops and the tank are simplified. Not built: the cooking shelter, net mound and kayaks (IMG_2619), the slot drains (IMG_2610, IMG_2630, IMG_2631), and the temporary sandbags.

nodes.name: North pool lawn
nodes.source: IMG_2204 and IMG_2205 (solved station camera) show lawn all round the pool deck. Its north and west sides follow the crazy-paving path's pool-side edge, its east side Calle Isabel, its south side the two hedges, both cast through the camera (2026-11-15). The aerial's dark band south of these hedges was the hedges themselves, read as grass, so the earlier aerial trace ran 3-5 m too far south. What lies south of the hedges is not seen. The measured deck is cut out. Good to about half a metre near the camera, a metre on the north side. 2026-11-15: the north edge moved 0.8-2.7 m north to the grass edge photographed in IMG_2205 (cast through its solved camera), between the deck and the path.

nodes.name: North pool · crazy-paving lawn-edge path
nodes.source: Photo-supported: irregular pale stone paving follows the curved retaining frontage at the northwest and the lower plinths across the north side, flush with the lawn (IMG_2204-2206, 2208). Estimated: 0.96 m width and exact plan curve (about +-2 m registration). Moved 2026-11-14 from data/north_pool_gardens.json as the centreline of its traced band. IMG_2204 shows the paving continuing down the west side along the curved white wall and along the south side behind the hedges; those continuations are not traced yet (task ground-plan-north-pool). 2026-11-15, through the solved IMG_2204 camera (pixels on the paving cast onto the surveyed ground): the west side runs at the foot of the curved white wall, about 1.4 m east of the earlier band (which projected onto the wall top); at the south-west corner it runs east to the tip of the hibiscus hedge and turns south along the hedge's west side out of view (stones at the photo's lower left); a second short path leaves the lawn south through the gap between the hibiscus hedge and the long south hedge. The north stretch is kept against the north patio fronts: cast through the same camera it lands 1-3 m further north, which would put it inside the patios (and the tree beside it casts 2 m north of where it stands against the paving), so the camera's far casts are taken as off and this is an open discrepancy, not a correction. 2026-11-15, re-traced with the north patios through the solved IMG_2205 camera (IMG_2204 as cross-check): the north stretch runs at the foot of the plinth wall, 0.7-2.4 m north of where it was, with the lawn's north edge at the photographed grass edge; this resolves the earlier north discrepancy (the patio fronts it was kept against were themselves traced too far south). Width 1.3 m for the whole path (the north side measures about 1.1-1.7 m between wall foot and grass).

nodes.name: Calle Isabel's crazy-paving surface beside the north pool lawn
nodes.source: IMG_2205 (solved station camera) shows the lane down the east side of the lawn paved in the same irregular stone as the lawn-edge path, not terracotta tiles: its west edge, cast through the camera onto the surveyed ground, runs at x -165.9 from z 9.5 to 18 (within 0.3-0.6 m of the mapped lane's west edge), and it reappears beyond the yucca bending south-east (about -163.8, 21.8 to -163.3, 22.6). The east edge is hidden by the yucca, so the surface takes the mapped lane's paved width with its margin (1.32 m), raised 0.21 m to lie just over the lane's own tiles (lanes are drawn 0.27 m over the ground). The lane's line and level stay those of data/street_layout.json; this is its surface. 15 Nov: the south bend moved about 0.5 m east so the yucca, whose trunk base casts to (-164.2, 22.5), stands on the lawn at the lane's edge as in IMG_2205.

Measured through the solved IMG_2206 camera on vertical wall planes: the west wall (x -187, the generated garden-wall line, which projects onto it) stands 1.9 m with a 1.0 m gate centred at z 31.1; the east wall runs from about (-183.1, 30.1) south-south-east past its gate (centred at (-182.37, 31.22)) towards the block by the camera, the direction on which that gate measures a usual 0.88 m wide and the wall top falls towards the camera as photographed (IMG_2208 shows the same wall). Estimated: the walls' ends and the patio's north and south sides, which are unseen.

The phones' camera pins disagree with the building polygons by several metres, so this is provisional plan geometry, NOT a solved-camera or surveyed trace. Do not infer public access through private gates, unseen walls or house footprints. Verify the path ends, widths and corner shape against additional ground-level photos before placement approval.
